title: LAMB: Latent Multi-Hypothesis Beliefs for Long-Horizon Large Language Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.26955v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-horizon language agents require compact memories that retain interaction evidence while preserving competing hypotheses about unobserved states. Although effective, many belief-state methods encode memory in discrete natural language, where repeated compression can omit evidence or prematurely discard plausible alternatives. We introduce LAMB, a recurrent framework for latent multi-hypothesis beliefs. A Common--Delta factorization combines a shared Common state for interaction evidence with weighted Delta components for competing hypotheses. Relative evidence from action-outcome predictions guides recurrent hypothesis updates without generating textual memory. A context-conditioned readout exposes hypotheses separately to the policy through a fixed-token belief prefix in the default configuration. translated_title: LAMB：面向长时程大语言智能体的潜在多假设信念
translated_abstract: 长时程语言智能体需要紧凑的记忆，既要保留交互证据，又要维持关于未观测状态的多个竞争性假设。尽管现有信念状态方法行之有效，但许多方法以离散自然语言编码记忆，反复压缩可能导致证据遗漏或过早丢弃合理的备选假设。我们提出LAMB，一个用于潜在多假设信念的循环框架。Common-Delta分解将共享的Common状态（用于存储交互证据）与加权的Delta组件（用于表示竞争性假设）相结合。来自动作-结果预测的相对证据引导假设的循环更新，而无需生成文本记忆。在默认配置中，上下文条件化的读出机制通过固定token的信念前缀将各个假设分别呈现给策略。信念模块与策略通过动作模仿以及辅助的状态、结果和观测判别目标进行联合训练。
tldr: 提出LAMB框架，通过潜在空间中的Common-Delta分解机制将交互证据与竞争性假设分离表示，使长时程语言智能体无需生成文本记忆即可高效维持多假设信念。
en_tdlr: LAMB introduces a recurrent latent multi-hypothesis belief framework with Common-Delta factorization, enabling long-horizon language agents to preserve interaction evidence and competing hypotheses in latent space without generating textual memory.
